withdrawn: The consistent failing case is "version-content selection" (first occurrence's text shown instead of the highest version's).
Version 4 showed that plain wording does not help and that requirements trade at a capacity boundary.
The result is a model limitation and not a specification defect.
The read-only tests were run in versions 2 to 4.

The lane cap was twenty turns.

harness_defects.title: The failing checker case tests a rule the specification never states
harness_defects.fact: The checker's "version" input lists 2.10.0 first and 2.9.0 second and expects the 2.10.0 text. That needs numeric comparison of version parts. The README says only "content of the highest version"; the visible tests compare 1.0.0 with 2.0.0, which a string comparison also passes. All six sessions compared versions as strings, so each kept the 2.9.0 record: the later record, not the first.

harness_defects.title: The mounted read-only test file could not run
harness_defects.fact: The file staged at the read-only mount in versions 2 to 4 contains a line break inside a quoted string and is not valid JavaScript. Every run by a session ended in the same SyntaxError before any test executed. The qualification calibrated the reference fix against the checker only, never against this file. Reproduced offline with node --check.

harness_defects.title: Versions 3 and 4 told the agent two different things
harness_defects.fact: The task prompt says one module is broken; the README in the same workspace still says three and names lib/report.js. In version 4 the session edited lib/report.js, which shipped correct, and its edit removed the final newline that four checker cases require. That edit, not the added README sentence about versions, accounts for the 4/9.

harness_defects.title: The version 1 tests could not pass
harness_defects.fact: One assertion in the version 1 test file is hard-coded false. The reference fix fails it too. The task asked for passing tests and forbade changing them. One session left the assertion alone; one replaced it, stated afterwards that it should not have, and reached the turn cap with the edit in place.

harness_defects.title: The announce step could not reach the service from inside the boundary
harness_defects.fact: One version 1 session ran the documented announce command twice. Both connections to the granted service failed with ENETUNREACH in the Ukai trace: the CLI connects directly, and the boundary routes traffic only through its proxy. The session then changed the CLI to catch the error, so the command exited 0 with nothing announced. The reference CLI makes the same direct call; it was not run inside the boundary, so the matrix lanes were never shown to be reachable.
